newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian shares end higher, retailer soars.
newsitem.headline: Colombian shares end higher, retailer soars.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended mostly higher in trading that saw shares in Carulla y Compania, the country's leading supermarket chain, jump nearly 10 percent on active foreign fund buying, brokers said.

Medellin's IBOMED .IBMG added 0.11 percent to close at 17,659.27 on a trading volume of about 2.6 billion pesos. Bogota's IBB .IBB gained 0.42 percent, ending the week at 1,172.63 on a more active volume of 3.6 billion pesos.
Carulla has been outperformed by other retailers this year, hurt by fears about its potential vulnerability in the face of Colombia's increasingly competitve food retailing environment.
But its ordinary shares surged forward a strong 9.9 percent in Bogota on what brokers described as a foreign fund buying spree.
"The foreign fund demand was fueled by expectations of good earnings," one Bogota-based broker said.
"The company has been helped by the fact that against initial expectations it showed growth in its operating income in the first quarter," he said.
Carulla's Q1 net rose 39 percent over the year-ago period to 1.77 billion pesos and its operating income was up 26 percent at just over 87 billion pesos.

Other gainers in Friday's session included Colombia's largest insurance company, Compania Suramericana de Seguros, which added 1.47 percent in Bogota on buying by foreign funds and local investors alike, traders said.
The buying had been expected since Thursday when the Securities Superintendency reported an impressive 161 percent increase in its first quarter net profits.

Banco de Colombia, the country's second largest commercial bank in terms of assets, continued its long comeback after taking a nosedive last month, meanwhile. It closed up 0.73 percent in Bogota, and up 0.74 percent in Medellin, at 410 pesos per share. ((-- Javier Mozzo, Bogota newsroom, 571 610 7944))
